answer: Alternative mutual funds may use complex strategies such as short selling or derivatives. Some use “absolute return” or “market neutral” approaches that seek positive returns even when stock markets fall. These strategies do not remove risk: depending on the approach, a fund may face additional risks involving derivatives, leverage, futures contracts, short selling, or swaps. Complex strategies may also lead to higher costs than those of traditionally managed funds.
